verdict.reasoning: Patient reports diarrhea for about three days and going to the toilet 5–6 times daily with watery loose stools: "I've been having, uh, diarrhoea, for like, let's say past three days" and "around, five to six times a day" and "it's definitely, definitely watery, uh, loose stools".

Patient states symptoms started with vomiting a couple of times which then stopped: "it started like three days ago. And uh, uh, so it started with vomiting, so I vomited a couple of times. Uh, but then, that went away, and, uh, yeah it's just diarrhoea now."

No blood in stools and no tummy pain reported: "Any blood in your stools?" Patient: "No, not that I could see." and "with the diarrhea have you noticed any other symptoms, like tummy pain?" Patient: "Uh, not, not really, no."
Patient describes feeling dehydrated and weak: "I feel like, um, I can't, really drink too much, so I feel very dehydrated" and later "I feel very weak though."

Patient has poor appetite and minimal solid intake: "Have you managed to eat anything, solids?" Patient: "Uh, not much, not much. So just a little bit, but I don't feel, um, I don't really feel like, uh, I have appetite."

Patient felt a bit feverish initially but not now: "probably at, at the beginning I was feeling I had a bit of temperature, but now I feel, I feel kind of fine." This supports initial feverish feeling and currently afebrile by history.
Patient reports asthma: "Um, so I, I do suffer of asthma. So, I do have my inhalers".
Patient uses a blue inhaler as needed, consistent with Salbutamol: "I do have my inhalers, uh, that I... use infrequently" and doctor clarifies "Is that the blue inhaler?" Patient: "Yes it is, yeah."
No known drug allergies: "Do you have any allergies to medications?" Patient: "Um, not that I know of."
Father had high blood pressure and died of bowel cancer: "my father has, high uh, well used to have high blood pressure. He actually... died, of, bowel cancer, like ten years ago."
Mother has type 2 diabetes: "Ohh yes, so uh, probably is worth mentioning uh, she has diabetes." Doctor: "Do you know if that's type one or type two?" Patient: "Uh, it's type two."

Patient lives alone and works as a software engineer: "Who lives at home with you, sir?" Patient: "Ohh I, I live alone." and later "What's your employment? What do you do for work?" Patient: "I'm a software engineer."
Patient does not smoke and drinks alcohol socially: "Do you do either of those?" (smoking and alcohol) Patient: "Uh, not really, I drink infrequently, like socially let's say, and I don't smoke."

Doctor diagnoses gastroenteritis: "I think you're probably suffering from what we call gastroenteritis" but the transcript does not explicitly state severity or label dehydration as 'mild'; 'mild dehydration' is an inferred qualifier not documented.

Doctor advises increased fluids and mentions Dioralyte: "you can drink plenty of fluids" and "you can get things from the pharmacy, which is called Dioralyte, which can help replenish any uh minerals and vitamins you may have lost... it's a type of fluid replacement drink."
Paracetamol advised as needed for feverish/weak feelings: "you can take some Paracetamol if you're feeling feverish and weak."

Rest and off work until diarrhea-free 24–48 hours: "I would probably advise you to continue taking time off work for next day or two, until you get better" and "normally you have to be diarrhea-free for about twenty four to forty eight hours, before you return back to work."

Transcript only states: "Let's see how the next few days go. And if you're still not better next week, I want you to come back and see me." It does not mention a specific 5-day threshold, worsening symptoms, or red-flag features like blood in stool or persistent vomiting as explicit return precautions.
